newsitem.title: USA: Brent heads south in late U.S. paper trading.
newsitem.headline: Brent heads south in late U.S. paper trading.

text.p: North Sea Brent headed south in late U.S. paper trading amid continued wide perceptions of plentiful physical supplies, traders said.
A series of partial May Brent cargoes changed hands at between $18.08 and $18.15 a barrel, down from the settlement of $18.19 on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE).
Intermonth spreads were quiet, though talk reinforced the market's steepening contango.
April/May Brent was pegged at around minus 65 cents, while May/June was assessed at minus 26-24 cents a barrel. June/July was at minus 14-12 cents.
